title: Projective edge of the resolution Hom double complex is a quasi-isomorphism
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $X,M$ be $R$-modules. Let $P_\bullet\to X$ be a nonnegative projective resolution (each $P_i$ projective and the augmented chain complex exact), and let $M\to E^\bullet$ be an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Form the first-quadrant double complex $K^{i,j}=\operatorname{Hom}_R(P_i,E^j)$, with horizontal differential precomposition by $d_P$ and vertical differential postcomposition by $d_E$, and total complex [def-sp-double-complex-total] with differential $d_h+(-1)^i d_v$. The canonical cochain map $\operatorname{Hom}_R(P_\bullet,M)\to\operatorname{Tot}(K)$ whose component in degree $n$ is postcomposition by $M\to E^0$ followed by inclusion of the $(n,0)$ summand is a quasi-isomorphism, meaning it induces an isomorphism on every cohomology module.

source.place: Tag 0954, proof of Lemma 47.8.2, Ext computed by an injective resolution; explicit double-complex comparison

proof.text: Construct the reversed projective complex in the opposite module category, apply linearCoyoneda as a bifunctor and take its total. Define both edge maps using the (n,0) and (0,n) inclusions. Check the chain-map equations: the unwanted differential is zero by the augmentation equation; the other is the Hom differential. Define precomposition maps and prove their two edge squares using associativity and compatibility with the augmentation. All constructions and squares are proved in Lean.

For each projective P_n, the linear Coyoneda functor preserves limits, since its composite with the faithful forgetful functor is representable. Projectivity makes that composite preserve epimorphisms. Reflection transfers this property to linear Coyoneda, which consequently preserves homology. Apply it to the quasi-isomorphism M[0]→E. Identify its source with Hom(P_n,M)[0] by the map which is identity in degree zero and between zero objects in positive degrees; prove this map is an isomorphism componentwise. This yields each vertical-column quasi-isomorphism. The argument is proved from Mathlib in Lean.

Flip K and use total symmetry with coefficient (-1)^(ij). Compose the projective edge with the inverse symmetry isomorphism; on (n,0) its sign is one. Thus it is the augmentation in the cited column criterion, with the preceding column quasi-isomorphisms. Apply that criterion and cancel the symmetry isomorphism to obtain the projective edge quasi-isomorphism.
